title: Tofu Larb
servings: Serves 2–3 as a main, 4–5 as part of a shared meal

items: 2 tbsp neutral oil (rice bran or grapeseed preferred)
1 ½ tbsp Thai fish sauce (or light soy sauce for vegetarian)
1 sprig culantro (optional, for authentic Northeastern aroma)
1 small handful coriander leaves (cilantro), roughly chopped
Crisp lettuce or cabbage leaves (for wrapping)
Long beans or cucumbers (as cooling sides)

instructions.title: 1. Prepare the tofu
steps: Drain tofu well, then crumble by hand or with a fork into small, irregular pieces (like minced meat).
Heat oil in a wok or skillet over medium-high.
Add tofu and cook until golden and slightly crisp at the edges, about 6–8 minutes. Remove from heat.

instructions.title: 2. Season the larb
steps: While tofu is still warm, add toasted rice powder, chili flakes, fish sauce (or soy), lime juice, and optional palm sugar.
Mix gently but thoroughly so every piece is coated. Adjust seasoning: more lime for sourness, more fish sauce for salt, more chili for heat.

instructions.title: 3. Add herbs & aromatics
steps: Fold in sliced shallots, spring onion, coriander, mint, and optional culantro/Thai basil.
Toss lightly to preserve the freshness of the herbs.

instructions.title: 4. Serve immediately
steps: Present in a chilled bowl or on a platter with crisp lettuce leaves, cabbage, and raw vegetables.
Traditionally enjoyed with warm sticky rice.

tips: Rice powder: Toast raw sticky rice in a dry pan until deep golden, then grind to a coarse powder for a nutty aroma.
Heat control: A top Thai restaurant larb is fiery but balanced—use roasted chili flakes for depth, not raw powder.
Texture contrast: Keep tofu slightly crisp; pair with cold, crunchy vegetables for the classic Isaan feel.
Plating: Serve in a wide shallow bowl, herbs fanned on top, with side vegetables neatly arranged. A dusting of extra toasted rice adds fragrance at the table.
